note: The decisions AWK-59's migration executes, separated from the script that
applies them. Read by backfill_seasons.py, asserted by season-orchestras.test.ts.
Everything here is a DECISION, not a derivation. Which orchestras held a
Season, and which years it spans, are computed live from bso-graph.json --
deliberately, because those facts already exist there and a second copy is a
second thing to drift. What lives here is what the graph cannot answer: the
two Seasons it holds no dated concert for, the cancelled year, the label
format, and the Long Island Youth Orchestra numbering, which has no source in
this repository at all.
THE INVARIANT THIS EXISTS TO PROTECT is (institution, number). Contentful
cannot express it -- space-wide uniqueness only, the same wall ADR-0008 hit
with (composer, slug) -- so it is asserted in the test instead. It is NOT
asserted in the build: ADR-0006 keeps `season` out of loadArchive(), and
adding a fetch for data no route renders would trade a real cost for a
theoretical one.
`label` is the season type's displayField, so it is what every entry picker
shows. It must therefore say which institution a Season belongs to: two
entries already carry number 29, one Brooklyn and one LIYO, and a picker
showing `Season 29` twice is unusable.
The year span is read from the Concert dates, never computed from the
number. See `cancelled` for why that distinction is load-bearing.
A HYPHEN, not an en dash. participation-checklist.md writes its own season
headings as `Season 29 - 2001-2002` with an en dash; this does not, because
this string is matched by pattern in both the applier and the test, and a
mistyped en dash is invisible in review.
`BSO` names the Brooklyn lineage, not only its current orchestra. Seasons
1-52 are one continuous numbering carried across two renamings, so Season 1
is a Brooklyn Heights Music Society year and is still labelled `BSO Season
1`. That is the orchestra's own convention: it counts 2025-2026 as its 52nd
season, which is only true if it claims 1973-1974 as its first.
The `orchestras` field on each entry records which orchestra actually held
the year, so the label's prefix never has to carry that.
The eras, as the graph has them: BHMS holds Seasons 1-5 (15 concerts,
to 2001-05-24), BSO holds Seasons 29-52 (127 concerts, 2001-11-08 to
2026-06-14). Only Season 5 is held by two, and see `knownLiveErrors` for
why Season 28 is not.
The only two Seasons whose year no source in this repository supports.
Both carry a `why` because a hand-assigned value with no reasoning is
indistinguishable from a typo six months later.
sea-1 omits `orchestras` on purpose: it HAS a concert, undated, and that
concert names BHMS. The orchestra is derivable; only the year is not.
Writing the orchestra here too would replace a fact with an opinion.

why: No dated concert. Season 2 opens 1974-11-20, and every adjacent season
steps by exactly one year, so Season 1 is 1973-1974. This also agrees with
the orchestra's own count of 2025-2026 as its 52nd season.
Its single concert is undated but names BHMS, so the orchestra is derived.
No concerts at all -- the entry's own `notes` field reads `LOST`. Season 10
closes 1982-12-14 and Season 12 opens 1984-10-23, both at BHO, so Season 11
is 1983-1984 and was held by BHO.
This is the one row where BOTH the year and the orchestra are assigned
rather than derived, because the graph holds nothing to derive from.
The live space links the 2001-05-24 concert to Brooklyn Symphony
Orchestra. Three sources disagree with it: bso-graph.json (from the
spreadsheet), the entry's OWN title -- which still reads `2001-05-24 —
BHO` -- and participation-checklist.md. Alex settled it on 2026-08-29:
the link is wrong.
It matters here because deriving `orchestras` from the live space rather
than from the graph would make Season 28 look like it straddles the BHO
to BSO renaming. It does not. Only Season 5 straddles, and the BSO name
begins at Season 29 on 2001-11-08.
The derivation therefore reads bso-graph.json, never the live space. This
row exists so the discrepancy is not rediscovered as a surprise, and so
the bad link got fixed rather than quietly ratified by a migration.
FIXED 2026-08-29. The live space now derives the same single straddling
season the graph does. Kept here rather than deleted: the reasoning is
what stops someone re-importing the error and concluding Season 28
straddles after all.
NOTE THE IDENTIFIER. This entry is NOT `cnc-20010524`. The importer remaps
graph ids onto live ones whenever a match key hits an existing entry, and
this concert lives under a Contentful auto-id -- participation.test.ts
records 33 concerts in that state. A concert IS its date here, which is
what import_to_contentful.py match_key and participation.json both key on.
The first attempt at this fix fetched the graph id and got a 404.
Never fixed by backfill_seasons.py, which writes season entries only.
The season was cancelled and consumed no season number. Season 47 is
2019-2020 and Season 48 is 2021-2022. Season 47's own `notes` field records
it: `SUSPENDED; 2020-2021 SEASON CANCELED, DUE TO COVID-19 PANDEMIC`.
This is why the year is read from Concert dates and never computed. An
offset from the number is correct for 47 consecutive seasons and wrong for
the last five -- a shape that survives every spot-check anyone would think
to run, and then misdates a fifth of the archive.

note: Stated by Alex on 2026-08-29 from direct knowledge. NOTHING in this
repository corroborates it: the Long Island Youth Orchestra has no concerts
in bso-graph.json, none in the source spreadsheet, and one photographed
program in docs/archive/. It is primary testimony, recorded as such.
Alex played every Concert of Seasons 29 to 32. The years below run one per
season with no gap, which is what he described.
DO NOT turn this into a formula. The offset that fits these four also fits
the Brooklyn seasons right up until it doesn't -- and unlike Brooklyn, there
is no LIYO concert data here that would ever catch a gap year. Four stated
values are worth more than a rule that looks right.
Seasons 30, 31 and 32 have no entry in the space yet. The applier reports
them as missing rather than creating them: creating an entry is a different
act from correcting one, and belongs to the data-entry pass.

existingEntry.label: LIYO 1991-1992
why: Created by hand by Alex during manual data entry, and never published.
The Delivery API serves published entries only, so this one was invisible
to the first survey of this migration -- which reported 52 seasons and no
LIYO, and was wrong on both counts.
The applier leaves its draft state alone. Publishing is a separate
decision and a season entry renders nothing either way.
